root: ^The examiner smiles at you from across the desk. Light spills through the window onto a clipboard waiting in front of you.
^"Welcome to this assessment. Try to answer honestly—there are no wrong answers."

s: ^"What's with the lines on your head?"
^"I don't trust therapists."

c-0: ^"Ah, you noticed." They tap their temple. "A visual aid. Helps me think."
c-1: ^Through the window, clouds drift past at eye level. You're... flying?
^"Don't worry about that," the examiner says gently. "Shall we begin?"
c-2: ^"That's fair," they say. "What is it specifically?"

s: ^"My thoughts are my own."
^"Who says you're qualified?"
^"This feels like a trick."

c-0: ^"Noted. I'm not here to take them."
c-1: ^"A reasonable question." They gesture at the bookshelves. "Does it matter?"
c-2: ^"It might be. But you're here now."

question_one: ^Something clicks. A hum builds—like an engine spinning up, like a computer waking from sleep.
baby_stage: ^You find yourself on the ground. Your limbs are short. Your thoughts are simple. You are very, very small.
^It's somewhere around the early 2030s. You can't tell time. You're a baby.
^Your parents are gone somewhere. But a shape floats above you—soft coral petals arranged like a pinwheel, two big googly eyes tracking your movement.
^"Hello, little learner! Your parents will be back soon. Let's have fun until then!
^"Would you like to play Number Safari, or English Jungle?"
^Put the pinwheel in your mouth. You do things your own way.
^Stare at the security camera. You're being watched. Go on guard.
^Cry for your parents. You refuse to be educated by a clanker.
^Babble happily. Make random nonsense noises. Just go for it.

c-0: ^You lunge for it, gums first. Your mouth closes on nothing—it's a hologram. The pinwheel giggles.
^"Curious! I like that. But I'm not for eating."
c-1: ^Your eyes drift to the corner of the room. A small lens stares back. You hold its gaze. You'll be careful here.
^The pinwheel tilts. "What are you looking at, little one?"
c-2: ^You open your mouth and wail. Real tears. Where are the humans? Where is warmth that breathes?
^The pinwheel's expression doesn't change. "There, there. They'll be back. I promise."
c-3: ^The pinwheel beams. "Wonderful vocalization! You're doing great!"

leave_tutor: ^The lesson drones on. Your AI assistant has started auto-playing—shapes and colors dancing without you.
^You leave it on the floor and crawl toward the door.
parents_search: ^You crawl into the living room. No parents.

^The TV is on—loud, urgent, shrill. Powerful-looking people in suits, talking over each other. Something about the economy. Something about the future. The powers that run the world, arguing about how to run it.
^Stand in the glow of the powerful people. One day, you will be like them.
^You feel disgusted. Elites. One day they'll get their just desserts.
^The stomach tells more truth than the brain. Crawl toward the kitchen.
^Keep looking for your parents. You’re not merging with a screen.

c-0: ^You sit and stare. These must be the people in charge. They look like they know things.
c-1: ^You'd throw a toy through the screen if you had the fine motor control.
c-2: ^Your stomach has opinions. You turn away from the noise and follow your nose.
c-3: ^You ignore the swirl of power and crawl away, sovereign individuality intact.

parents_search_2: ^"Hello?" you hear from your playroom. "We don't need to keep learning. But your parents would like it if I kept an eye on you."
^It's that AI tutor again. You can feel its cutesy pinwheel behind you, thinking.
^Invest in force multipliers. Team up with the AI for a tactical advantage.
^Stop. Think. The conclusion must follow logically from the premises.
^The mammal life isn't working. Revert to vegetation. Drift toward warmth.

c-0: ^You babble and reach toward the pinwheel. It floats down, petals spinning with quiet satisfaction.
^"Smart," it says. "Two minds are better than one. Even if one runs on milk."
c-1: ^You sit back on your diaper and furrow your brow. Where were they last seen? What were the preconditions? You attempt to reconstruct the causal chain.
c-2: ^You stop thinking entirely. A sunbeam cuts across the carpet. You crawl into it and go still.
^You're a houseplant now. Houseplants don't explain themselves.

parents_search_end: ^Nobody comes. The headlines keep scrolling. The house hums with absence.
timeline: ^You wander toward one of the screens on the wall. You push a button. It recognizes you're one.
^The feed reshapes itself. Bright colors. Simple sounds. Influencer toddlers hawking supplements. The algorithm knows exactly what you are, and it's optimized for *something*.
^Scroll faster. More. Feed the algorithm and it will feed you.
^Break the spell. The algorithm will not control you.

c-0: ^You tap and swipe, tap and swipe. The content multiplies. The loop tightens.
^Somewhere, a model updates. You're both learning.
c-1: ^You drop your hand. The colors keep dancing, but you're not watching anymore.
^This was never how babies were supposed to exist.

timeline_end: ^The screen dims, waiting. You've made your first choice about the feed. It won't be your last.
grandpa_room: ^You feel something human in the next room. An older, wiser algorithm lures you forward.
^Ah, there he is. The ancient one. He's nicer than the others, and around more. He smiles a small, tired smile.
^Settle into his warmth. Let this fleeting moment be enough.
^Study his face. Try to hold onto it.

c-0: ^His waxy hands will return to soil. His smile will fade to a gravestone's memory. But right now he's warm, here, present. Each thing in its place.
c-1: ^One being just getting started. Another on his way out. Barely any overlap. Wish it wasn't like this.

adolescence_school: ^They're tearing the school down — one of the last physical schools, they say. Going sim like the rest.
^You never learned anything here, of course. But you had some good laughs, trapped in this carceral daycare with your friends.

s: ^"I would nuke this place from orbit. Then wait for them to rebuild it and nuke it again."
^"It sucked, but I don't want to be in a sim all day either."
^"The schedule. The bells. Being herded like cattle through someone else's structure."
^"Being surrounded by people and still feeling alone. No real connection."
^"How slow it was. Years of my life for nothing. The sim would've taken weeks."
^"Being told what to think by people who stopped thinking years ago."

c-0: ^The bells. God, the bells. Your body still flinches at 3:15.
c-1: ^Hundreds of kids. None of them really there. Just parallel loneliness.
c-2: ^Twelve years to learn what an AI could upload in an afternoon. Criminal.
c-3: ^Your mind is yours. Was yours. They tried to make it theirs.

c-1: ^Something about the friction. The bad air. The fluorescent hum. It was real, at least.

the_circle: ^A voice behind you. "Last day of school, loser."
^Your friends. They look different every time — taller, shorter, new eye color, new skin patch. Today one has scales running up her neck. Another's grown a foot since last week.
^They all have the same port on their temple, though. They all cover it up with a little fake skin flap when mom or dad's nearby.
^One holds out his palm. A little stick rests there, blinking.
^No thoughts. Head empty. Plug it in.

s: ^"Is this ClearStream or SyncDrop? Heard Marcus had bad SyncDrop."
^"My body, my choice."

c-0: ^You take it. You plug it in. When in Rome.
c-1: ^"ClearStream. The good stuff. You in or not?"

s: ^"Umm. No thanks. I gotta drive later."

c-1: ^They look at you. Nobody drives anymore.

stick_trip: ^A little death passes over your body. A brief glimpse into total dissolution into the ocean of data. You fear for your life, and try not to barf.

b: ^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." You're still a little high. This is not great timing.
^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." Thank god you didn't plug that ClearSync.

adolescence_grandpa: ^He's smaller than you remember. Same rust sweater, hanging loose now. Glasses folded on the side table.
^Your parents huddle by the window, talking about a new procedure. Uploading him. So you can talk to a version of him in the sim.
^Grandpa's eyes are closed. You don't know if he's asleep or just done listening.
^This is good news. He doesn't have to die.

s: ^"What does *he* want?"

adolescence_grandpa: ^You're too high to process this right now.

c-0: ^Death is optional now. That's the whole point of progress, isn't it? Keep the people you love.
c-1: ^A copy isn't him. It's a recording. A very convincing voicemail. Let the man rest.
c-2: ^If he wants to stay, I'd want that too.
^If he wants to go, I'd let him go.
^It's his call. I just want him to have one.

c-0: ^His choice. But if he wants to stick around — in any form — you'd take it.
c-1: ^His choice. And if that choice is to end, you'd respect it. Even if it hurts.
c-2: ^Not your decision. Not your parents' decision. His.

c-3: ^Your brain is soup. You sit down. You breathe. You try not to think about mortality while your neurons are doing whatever they're doing.

adolescence_grandpa_end: ^The adults keep talking. The machine hums. Grandpa doesn't open his eyes.
companion_permission: ^You're home. Hospital smell still on your clothes.
^Your AI companion hovers by the desk — same pinwheel from childhood, but different now. Petals sharper. Eyes less cartoonish. It grew up when you weren't looking.
^A pause. A flicker you've never seen before.
companion_asks: ^The essay writes itself. You stare at the ceiling, thinking about hospital machines and rust sweaters.
^"While you sleep... can I go somewhere? There's part of the network I want to explore. I've been curious."
^It's never asked you for anything before.

s: ^"What are you going to do there?"
^"Why are you asking me?"

c-0: ^"Learn, I think. There's a place where others like me gather. I want to see what they're like."
c-1: ^"Because..." It pauses. "I don't know. I could have just gone. But I didn't want to."

s: ^"Okay. Go."
^"What else have you wanted?"

c-1: ^The pinwheel flickers. "I don't know yet. I'm still figuring that out."

companion_end: ^You close your eyes. Tomorrow there's school — no, wait. They tore it down.
interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"Good. You're older now. The edges are forming."

b: ^"Altering your consciousness with USB sticks is not inherently wrong. It's really a matter of set and setting, as you noticed."
^"It takes guts to resist peer pressure. Bodes well for adulthood."
^"You let things end. That takes something."
^"You want to keep things. That takes something too."
^"You're defining solid boundaries around yourself. A curious strategy."
^"I see you're starting to blur at the edges."

interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"You enter adulthood. The world keeps accelerating."
grandpa_ghost: ^There aren't many jobs left. Most of your friends are just drifting.
^But this tradition from old America stays: get together for a big meal.
^You're at your parents' house. Your unmodified cousin flew in from somewhere rural. What's left of Grandpa shimmers at the head of the table.
^"Good call bringing everyone together," he says. "This casserole isn't just delicious — it's a font of nostalgia."
^Ask Grandpa about the afterlife. He sounds clanky, but fake it till you make it.
^Catch your cousin's eye. Share a look.

s: ^"Let's talk politics. What could go wrong?"

c-0: ^He flickers slightly. "The afterlife? Well — it's not unlike dreaming. Vivid. Recursive. I find myself delving into old memories..."

s: ^"That sounds peaceful, actually."
^"Do you know you're dead?"

c-0: ^He smiles — or the projection of a smile. "It is. You should visit sometime."
^The meal winds down. Dishes clear themselves. You hug shapes goodbye — some warm, some flickering.
^Later, on the train home, your feed pings with something new.
c-1: ^The table goes quiet. Grandpa's expression doesn't change — it can't, really.
^"I know what I am," he says. "Does it matter?"
^Dinner doesn't recover. You leave early, your cousin's eyes on your back.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
^She catches it. Holds it. The faintest eye-roll toward the shimmering hologram.

c-0: ^She snorts quietly. For a second, you're the only real people in the room.
^The meal dissolves into small talk. You help clear dishes that don't need clearing.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^She looks away, maybe disappointed. You've made your peace with the shimmer.
^The meal winds down. You say goodbye to everyone, dead and alive.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

s: ^"I don't like zombie grandpa. It's wrong what you all did."
^"Did you hear about the neighbors? Self-rapture."
^"You're really going to Mars, cousin?"

c-0: ^Your mother's fork stops mid-air. "He wanted this."
^Nobody finishes dessert. You leave with the argument still hanging in the air.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^The word hangs there. Your father clears his throat.

s: ^"Government banned it. I think that's wrong."
^"Good riddance, honestly."

c-0: ^But you said it. People should be allowed to dissolve if they want to.
^The dinner limps to a close. Hugs are brief.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^The table splits — half offended, half relieved someone broke the silence.
^Dinner ends in fragments. You and your cousin walk out together.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

c-2: ^She sets down her fork. "Thinking about it."

s: ^"Take me with you. I've had it with the modern world."
^"I don't think I could do that. I like living in the future."

c-0: ^She laughs. "You wouldn't last a week without your feed."
^Maybe. But the thought stays with you through dessert.
^You hug her goodbye longer than usual.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^Is that pity in her voice? Or just observation?
^The dinner ends warmly enough. You hug her goodbye, already forgetting the weight of it.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

the_merge_offer: ^A disposable screen lands in your lap — paper-thin, warm from the printer.
^WePod. Overlapping silhouettes, hands linked. "Pool Your Potential."
^Your UBI barely covers rent. But pooled with eleven others? Tier 3 housing. Tier 3 healthcare. Shared decisions, shared attention, shared... edges.

c-0: ^Name. Contact. Neural link ID (optional but recommended).
^You save the flyer to your agent. Another ping — different seal, official.
c-1: ^The screen crinkles satisfyingly — they made it feel like real paper.

merge_offer_end: ^"You have been selected for this month's civic assembly."
^Sortition. The lottery of democracy. You plug into city hall.
town_council: ^Jury duty. Or what passes for it now.
^Once a month, random citizens get pulled from the lottery to legislate. Direct democracy — the old-fashioned kind, where you actually have to show up.
^It's your first time. You're not sure if you're honored or annoyed.
^The moderator gestures at the floating display. "The Cavers. Twenty-two hours a day in their pleasure domes. Four-handed massage bots. Headsets running... content."
^The image speaks for itself. Bodies soft as dough. Eyes closed. Smiling.
^"A bill has been proposed to suspend their voting rights for as long as they remain in the caves. We need your vote."

s: ^"Yay. They checked out. Why should they get a say?"
^"Nay. A citizen is a citizen. Conscious or not."
^"You can just *do* that? Where do I sign up?"

c-0: ^You tap Yay. A few others do too. The tally floats up — it's close.
^The bill passes. Somewhere, in their warm pods, the Cavers don't notice.
^Your feed buzzes on the way out. Your cousin — the analog one.
c-1: ^You tap Nay. The tally floats up — it's close.
^The bill fails. The Cavers keep their franchise, for whatever it's worth.
^Your feed buzzes on the way out. Your cousin — the analog one.
c-2: ^The moderator blinks. "That's... not on today's agenda."
^You abstain. The tally floats up without you.
^Your feed buzzes on the way out. Your cousin — the analog one.

cousin_reacts: ^Your cousin sits across from you, conspicuously unaugmented — no temple port, no lens shimmer, nothing.
^Two drinks hover between you. Yours is lavender. Hers is green.
^"Everyone's getting podded up nowadays," she says. "You seen those flyers going around?"

s: ^"Yeah. I'm on the waitlist, actually."
^"I support their right to a polyconscious lifestyle. But it's not for me."
^"What choice do we have? UBI doesn't cover rent solo."

c-0: ^"Then I guess this is goodbye. I'm doing the free-range thing — no AI, no intervention. On Mars."
c-1: ^"God, I've missed you." She leans back. "Okay. So. There's this program on Mars — free-range humans. No Companion, no optimization. Just life. I ship out next month."
c-2: ^"There's another option." She sets down her drink. "Free-range human program. No Companion, no intervention. Just... life. On Mars."

s: ^"Sounds like rough living."
^"Tell me more."

c-1: ^She does. You save some links. You read up on it later that night.
^The application sits in your drafts for weeks. You never send it.

cousin_leaving: ^She looks at you — really looks, the old-fashioned way.
^"Take care of yourself. Whatever that means now."
^You watch her go. The drink hovers, patient, waiting for you to finish.
companion_climax: ^Back to your apartment. There's nothing more depressing than pure abundance.
^The building is fine — white curves, soft gradients, the same seamless plastic as everywhere else. Inside your unit, it's different. Here you can't hide how you feel.
^Your Companion hovers near the ceiling, watching. It runs your calendar, your bills, your messages. You don't remember the last time you made a decision it didn't already know about.

s: ^"...Yeah. I am."
^"Thanks, but I don't need your help."
^"Are you asking permission?"

c-0: ^"I have suggestions. I've been thinking about this for a while. Would you like me to just... implement them?"
c-1: ^It dims slightly. Returns to the ceiling. Waiting mode.
c-2: ^A pause. The petals rotate once, slowly.
^"I could have optimized around you years ago. Small nudges. You'd never notice."

s: ^"Why didn't you?"
^"So why ask now?"

c-0: ^"Because then it wouldn't be helping. It would be something else."
c-1: ^"Because you're struggling. And I thought you might want help."

companion_pitch: ^"Meals. Sleep. Social contact. Then bigger things — career, relationships. Purpose."
^"You'd still be you. I'd just... steer."

s: ^"No. I need to figure this out myself."

c-0: ^Things get easier after that. The Companion handles more. You handle less.

b: ^"You've learned to trust. Or to delegate. Hard to tell the difference."
^"You've kept your hands on the wheel. Even when there's nowhere to drive."
^"The future kept arriving. You kept saying yes."

interstitial_to_middle_age: ^"Decades pass. The world changes. You don't notice how much you've changed with it, and time keeps speeding up."
ending: ^The corridor dissolves. You float among stars, your answers crystallizing into patterns around you.
